mainTopic: Signals for burning חמץ, and the משנה and גמרא on burning items of different levels of טומאה together
overview: This amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about two cows plowing on הר המשחה. The cows signaled when people could still eat חמץ, when they had to hold it, and when they had to burn it. Then a new משנה begins. רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים reports that the כהנים burned less-impure meat together with more-impure meat. רבי עקיבא adds a similar case of disqualified oil lit in an impure lamp. רבי מאיר learns from these cases that pure and impure תרומה may be burned together on ערב פסח. רבי יוסי rejects this, noting that even רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree they are burned separately and argue only about doubtful תרומה. The גמרא then explains רבי חנינא's case: the meat goes from שלישי to שני, and food passes impurity to food at least מדרבנן. Finally the גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא adds. רב יהודה begins to answer that the lamp is made of metal, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The two plowing cows as a public signal for eating, holding, and burning חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes describing a signal on הר המשחה. Two cows plowing meant the people could still eat חמץ. One cow removed meant they should hold the חמץ. Both removed meant they should burn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two cows would plow on הר המשחה. As long as both were plowing, all the people ate. Once one was taken away, they held their חמץ in waiting: no eating and no burning. Once both were taken away, all the people began burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that describes how people in ירושלים knew the exact time to stop eating חמץ and to burn it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three stages, and each has its own sign. Both cows plowing means you may eat. One cow removed means you stop eating but do not burn yet; the חמץ is held 'hanging' (תולין). Both removed means burn. This matches the earlier discussion about an in-between hour when you may not eat חמץ but do not yet have to destroy it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Mount of Olives, which could be seen from the city
Holding in suspense: not eating and not burning

steps.confusionAlert: תולין here does not mean 'hang up' literally. It means the חמץ is left in a waiting status: you may not eat it, but you also do not burn it yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a real-life picture of the middle hour on ערב פסח. In that hour חמץ may not be eaten but does not yet have to be destroyed.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁתֵּי פָרוֹת הָיוּ חוֹרְשׁוֹת בְּהַר הַמִּשְׁחָה.
phrases.english: Two cows would plow on the Mount of Olives.
As long as both of them are plowing —
all the people eat (חמץ).
When one of them is taken away — they hold it in suspense;
they neither eat nor burn.
When both of them were taken away —
all the people began burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּי פָרוֹת הָיוּ חוֹרְשׁוֹת בְּהַר הַמִּשְׁחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous daf about public signals for the deadlines of חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two cows plowing: eat. One removed: hold (no eating, no burning). Both removed: burn.

steps.title: The כהנים burned less-impure meat together with more-impure meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים testifies about the כהנים. They burned meat that touched a ולד הטומאה together with meat that touched an אב הטומאה. They did this even though it adds טומאה to the less-impure meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה begins. רבי חנינא, the deputy of the כהנים, says: In all the days of the כהנים, they never held back from burning meat that became impure through a secondary source of impurity together with meat that became impure through a primary source of impurity. They did this even though it adds more impurity to its impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. רבי חנינא reports that the כהנים burned two pieces of impure קדשים meat together, even though one would make the other more impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you may not make holy food more impure than it already is. But here both pieces are going to be burned anyway. So raising the level of the weaker piece causes no real loss, and the כהנים did it without worry. The key point is that both items are already impure; only the level changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה: marks the start of a new משנה
Adding impurity onto its existing impurity

steps.confusionAlert: Both pieces of meat are already impure. The משנה is not about making pure food impure. It only talks about raising an impure item to a higher level.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base case. Both רבי עקיבא and רבי מאיר build on it, and רבי יוסי argues that it cannot be stretched too far.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy of the priests, says:
In all the days of the priests
they did not hold back from burning the meat
that became impure through a secondary source of impurity
together with the meat that became impure through a primary source of impurity,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוֹסִיפִין טוּמְאָה עַל טוּמְאָתוֹ.
phrases.english: even though they add impurity to its impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים אוֹמֵר: מִימֵיהֶם שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים לֹא נִמְנְעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה. It connects to the topic of burning (חמץ of תרומה and קדשים) on ערב פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure meat that is going to be burned may be burned together with more-impure meat, even though this raises its level of טומאה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא adds the case of disqualified oil lit in an impure lamp
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא adds a parallel testimony. The כהנים lit תרומה oil that was made פסול by a טבול יום inside a lamp made impure by a טמא מת. This raised the oil's level of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא added and said: In all the days of the כהנים, they never held back from lighting oil that was disqualified by a טבול יום in a lamp that became impure through someone impure from a corpse. They did this even though it adds more impurity to its impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a second example of the same idea. This time it is oil and a lamp instead of meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil touched by a טבול יום is only at a very low level: it is פסול but not fully טמא. Putting it in a lamp that is a ראשון לטומאה raises it to a higher level. The case is still like רבי חנינא's: the oil was already unfit and is being used up (burned) anyway. So raising its level causes no loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who immersed today and is not fully pure until nightfall
Became disqualified (unfit, a low level of impurity)
Someone impure from contact with a corpse

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי עקיבא presents this as an addition to רבי חנינא's case. Later (step 19) the גמרא counts the levels, finds that it seems to be the same שלישי-to-שני change, and asks what רבי עקיבא is adding.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva added and said:
In all the days of the priests
they did not hold back from lighting the oil
that was disqualified through a טבול יום
in a lamp that became impure through one impure from a corpse,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמּוֹסִיפִין טוּמְאָה עַל טוּמְאָתוֹ.
phrases.english: even though they add impurity to its impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel case to רבי חנינא's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disqualified תרומה oil may be lit in an impure lamp, even though this raises the oil's level of טומאה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns that pure and impure תרומה may be burned together on פסח
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר draws a conclusion from the two testimonies. On ערב פסח, pure תרומה חמץ may be burned together with impure תרומה חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: From their words we learned that one may burn pure תרומה together with impure תרומה on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר takes the idea from the two earlier cases and applies it to burning חמץ of תרומה on ערב פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning: once the time to burn חמץ arrives, even the pure תרומה is going to be destroyed. So it does not matter if it becomes impure while being burned, just as it did not matter in the meat and oil cases. He treats 'about to be burned anyway' as the key factor.

keyTerms.meaning: From their words we learned (an inference)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling that ties the משנה back to פסח. Later in the sugya (on the following dappim, not on this amud), the גמרא will work to explain exactly which earlier case רבי מאיר is learning from.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
From their words we learned
that one burns pure teruma
together with the impure on Passover.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical inference from the two testimonies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב פסח, pure תרומה חמץ may be burned together with impure תרומה חמץ.

steps.title: רבי יוסי rejects רבי מאיר's comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says this is not a valid comparison. The earlier cases only raised the level of something already impure. רבי מאיר's case makes pure תרומה impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: That is not the right comparison.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי rejects רבי מאיר's inference. He says the earlier cases cannot teach the law about pure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי חנינא's and רבי עקיבא's cases, both items were already impure; only the degree went up. In רבי מאיר's case, a completely pure item would become impure. רבי יוסי sees that as a different and more serious step.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not the right measure, meaning the comparison does not work

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא and רבי עקיבא: you may make impure things more impure when they are being destroyed. רבי מאיר stretches this to making pure תרומה impure on ערב פסח. רבי יוסי says that stretch is invalid, because 'pure to impure' is not like 'impure to more impure'.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי מאיר's inference only. He does not reject the testimonies of רבי חנינא and רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The earlier cases only raised the level of something already impure. They cannot prove that you may make pure תרומה impure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵינָהּ הִיא הַמִּדָּה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said: That is not the (correct) comparison.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֵינָהּ הִיא הַמִּדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects רבי מאיר's inference in step 4.

steps.title: Both sides agree: pure and impure תרומה are burned separately
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי continues his rejection of רבי מאיר. He points out that רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע both agree that pure תרומה and impure תרומה must be burned separately on ערב פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree that you burn this one (the pure) by itself, and that one (the impure) by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי backs up his rejection of רבי מאיר. He cites a point that both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree on: pure תרומה may not be burned together with impure תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This agreement goes against רבי מאיר's view from step 4, since רבי מאיר allowed burning them together. Even רבי יהושע, the lenient one in the coming argument, will not make pure תרומה impure. רבי יוסי uses this as the proof for his rejection in step 5.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua agree
that one burns this (pure teruma) by itself
and that (impure teruma) by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי continues from step 5. He supports his rejection of רבי מאיר by citing the agreement of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע that pure תרומה is not made impure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pure תרומה and impure תרומה are burned separately. This is agreed by all.

steps.title: The argument about doubtful תרומה and impure תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue only about תרומה whose purity is in doubt, burned together with definitely impure תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they argue? About the doubtful תרומה and the impure תרומה. רבי אליעזר says: burn this by itself and that by itself. רבי יהושע says: both together.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains what the argument is about. The question is whether תרומה that might be pure may be burned together with תרומה that is surely impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה תלויה is in doubt. We may not eat it, but we also may not make it impure on purpose. רבי אליעזר treats it like pure תרומה, so it must be burned separately. רבי יהושע allows burning it together with the impure, because it is not definitely pure.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה 'hanging' in doubt, whose purity is uncertain

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees: definitely pure and impure תרומה are not burned together. The argument is only about doubtful תרומה burned with impure תרומה.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About the teruma in doubt and the impure teruma.
For Rabbi Eliezer says:
This should be burned by itself and that by itself,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says: both of them together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After stating the agreement, the משנה narrows down the exact point of the argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר says doubtful and impure תרומה are burned separately. רבי יהושע says they may be burned together.

steps.title: Where is the added impurity in the meat case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא's case. The weaker meat ends up a שני either way, so it is not clear how the meat gains more impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now consider: meat that became impure through a ולד הטומאה is what level? A שני. When you burn it with meat that became impure through an אב הטומאה, what does it become? A שני. It was a שני and stays a שני. So where is the 'adding impurity to its impurity'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by going back to רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים's testimony from step 2. It does the math and asks how this case really adds impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ולד הטומאה is a ראשון, a first-level impurity, so meat that touches it becomes a שני. Meat that touched an אב הטומאה is a ראשון, so when the weaker meat touches it, it again becomes a שני. Its level never changes, so the משנה's words 'adding impurity' seem not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Now consider. Opens a line of reasoning that leads to a question.
Adding impurity to its impurity, meaning raising its level

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that touching something 'more impure' always raises the level. An item becomes one level below whatever it touches. Touching a ראשון makes it a שני, no matter how impure the ראשון itself became.

phrases.english: GEMARA. Now consider:
meat that became impure through a secondary source of impurity
what is it? A second-level impurity.
phrases.notes: A ולד הטומאה is a ראשון, so whatever touches it becomes a שני.

phrases.english: When one burns it
together with meat that became impure through a primary source of impurity
what does it become? A second-level impurity.
phrases.notes: The other meat is a ראשון, so touching it makes a שני.

phrases.english: It was second and it is second.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי מוֹסִיף לוֹ טוּמְאָה עַל טוּמְאָתוֹ אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: What 'adding impurity to its impurity' is there?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי בָּשָׂר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּוְולַד הַטּוּמְאָה מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is done. The גמרא now goes back to analyze רבי חנינא's testimony from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording that רבי חנינא's case adds impurity to impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Working out the levels shows the weaker meat is a שני before and after. Nothing is added, which contradicts the משנה's description.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the meat was only a third-level impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains the case is about meat that touched a ולד of a ולד, so it is a שלישי. Burning it with the other meat raises it to a שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Here we are dealing with a ולד of a ולד, so the meat is a שלישי. רבי חנינא holds that it is permitted to make a שלישי into a שני.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by changing how we picture the case. The weaker meat is one level lower than we thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weaker meat touched something that was itself a שני, so the meat is only a שלישי. Burning it with the meat that touched an אב הטומאה, which is a ראשון, raises it to a שני. That is a real addition of impurity, and רבי חנינא holds this is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An offspring of an offspring of impurity, meaning it touched a שני

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא's case is about raising a שלישי to a שני. That is the 'adding impurity to impurity' that the כהנים allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the exact level change behind רבי חנינא's testimony. This matters for comparing it to רבי מאיר's ruling on burning תרומה חמץ.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Here we are dealing with an offspring of an offspring of impurity,
so it is a third-level impurity,
and he (Rabbi Chanina) holds that a third-level impurity
may be made into a second-level impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הָכָא בִּוְולַד וְולַד עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the weaker meat touched a ראשון and was already a שני, so nothing would be added.
steps.terutzMaskana: The weaker meat touched a שני and was a שלישי. Burning it with the ראשון meat raises it to a שני, so impurity really is added.

steps.title: But food does not make other food impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב יהודה's explanation. In his case, one piece of meat makes another piece of meat more impure, but there is a rule that food cannot pass impurity to food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a rule that food does not make other food impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of רב יהודה from Step 9. It points to a rule that seems to say his case cannot happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יהודה's case, the more impure meat raises the other meat from a שלישי to a שני. That means food is passing impurity to food. The גמרא says there is a known rule that food does not do this.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that…? (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But food does not make food impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer רב יהודה gave in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation that the שלישי meat becomes a שני when it is burned with the other meat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His explanation needs food to pass impurity to food, and a known rule says food cannot do that.

steps.title: The ברייתא source: food does not make similar food impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that learns from a פסוק that impure food does not make other food impure like itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: You might think that food makes food impure. So the Torah says, "If water is put on seed, and some of their carcass falls on it, it is impure." The food itself is impure, but it does not make something like it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for the rule it just used to challenge רב יהודה. The source is a ברייתא that reads a פסוק closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "it is impure," with the word הוּא ("it"). The ברייתא reads this as a limit: only the seed itself is impure, and it does not pass that impurity on to other food. This gives the challenge in Step 10 a firm source.
steps.confusionAlert: This rule does not say the food itself stays pure. The food itself is impure. The rule only says it cannot pass impurity on to other food.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
One might think that food makes food impure;
therefore the verse says:
"And if water is put on seed,
and some of their carcass falls on it, it is impure" —
it is impure,
phrases.notes: The word הוּא is read as a limit: only the seed itself.

phrases.english: but it does not make something like it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יְהֵא אוֹכֶל מְטַמֵּא אוֹכֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule used in the challenge of Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that food does not pass impurity to other food.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 11:38, focusing on the words "טָמֵא הוּא".

steps.title: According to אביי there is no problem
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, the rule only applies to חולין. In תרומה and קדשים, food does pass impurity to other food, so רב יהודה's case works.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to אביי, who said: They only taught this rule about חולין. But with תרומה and קדשים, food does make something like itself impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts checking which opinions have a problem with רב יהודה. It begins with אביי, who has no problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי limits the ברייתא to regular food (חולין). Holy foods are stricter, so with them food can pass impurity to food. Our case is about meat of קדשים, so the challenge does not hurt רב יהודה according to אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to… (the problem does not apply to this view)
Holy food, such as sacrifice meat

phrases.english: This works well according to Abaye, who said:
They taught this only regarding non-sacred food;
but with teruma and consecrated food —
it does make something like itself impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the challenge from the ברייתא does not apply according to אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא to חולין only.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule from the ברייתא applies to every kind of food.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to אביי, the rule applies only to חולין. Food in קדשים can pass impurity to other food, so רב יהודה's case stands.

steps.title: According to רב אדא בר אהבה there is also no problem
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה in the name of רבא says the rule applies to חולין and תרומה, but not to קדשים. Since our case is about קדשים, it works for him too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also according to רב אדא בר אהבה in the name of רבא, who said: They only taught this rule about חולין and תרומה. But with קדשים, food does make something like itself impure. So it works well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that also has no problem with רב יהודה. This prepares for the one opinion that does have a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view applies the rule to more foods than אביי does, since it also includes תרומה. But it still leaves out קדשים. Because our meat is קדשים, food can still pass impurity to food here.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Adda bar Ahava
in the name of Rava, also, who said:
They taught this only regarding non-sacred food and teruma;
but with consecrated food —
it does make something like itself impure — it works well.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא נָמֵי דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second view under which the challenge does not apply.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא to חולין and תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule from the ברייתא might include קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רב אדא בר אהבה, קדשים is left out of the rule, so רב יהודה's case about קדשים meat stands.

steps.title: According to רבינא the question remains
steps.stepSummary: רבינא in the name of רבא says the פסוק makes no exceptions. Even in קדשים, food does not pass impurity to food. So how can our משנה speak of adding impurity?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבינא in the name of רבא, who said: The פסוק spoke in full, with no exceptions. It makes no difference whether it is חולין, תרומה, or קדשים. In every case food does not make something like itself impure. What can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reaches the one opinion that does have a problem with רב יהודה. It asks what can be said according to רבינא. Steps 15 to 17 answer this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא holds that the rule from the ברייתא covers every food, even holy food. If so, the meat in רב יהודה's case cannot pass impurity to the other meat. Then it is hard to understand how the משנה can call this "adding impurity."

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק speaks in full, with no exceptions
What can be said? (asks for an answer according to this view)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רב יהודה's answer only works under some opinions. That pushes the גמרא to look for an explanation that fits רבינא too.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on whether food passes impurity to food. אביי says the rule is only for חולין. רב אדא בר אהבה says it is for חולין and תרומה. רבינא says it is for everything, even קדשים, and only רבינא's view causes trouble for רב יהודה.

phrases.english: But according to Ravina in the name of Rava, who said:
The verse spoke in a full, categorical way;

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא חוּלִּין, לָא שְׁנָא תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: no difference whether non-sacred food, no difference whether teruma,
no difference whether consecrated food —
it does not make something like itself impure.
What is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with Steps 12 and 13 by naming the view under which the challenge still applies.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's explanation, and the משנה's words about adding impurity, according to רבינא's view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If food never passes impurity to food, even in קדשים, then the meat cannot become more impure by being burned with other meat.

steps.title: The meat had liquids on it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers רבינא's challenge. The meat had liquids on it, and the liquids are what passed the impurity to the other meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where there are liquids together with the meat. The other meat becomes impure because of the liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה's reading of the משנה. It says the impurity passed through liquids that were on the meat, not from food to food directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food cannot make other food impure, but liquids can. If the meat that touched the אב הטומאה had liquids on it, the liquids made the second piece impure. This keeps the משנה from breaking the rule from the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a formula that narrows down the case)
Liquids, which can pass impurity to food

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where there are liquids together with the meat,
so it becomes impure because of the liquids.
phrases.notes: Liquids can pass impurity to food, even though food cannot pass it to food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of רבינא in the name of רבא by redefining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה describes food making food impure, which goes against the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liquids on the meat passed the impurity, so the rule is not broken.

steps.title: The משנה should have mentioned liquids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the liquids answer. If liquids were the key, the משנה should have said 'meat and liquids.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this phrase, 'with meat that became impure by an אב הטומאה,' should have said 'with meat and liquids'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The wording of the משנה does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the liquids are what pass the impurity, they are the most important part of the case. The משנה would not leave them out and mention only the meat. So the liquids answer does not match the משנה's words.

phrases.english: If so,
this phrase, "with meat that became impure by a primary source of impurity,"
should have said "with meat and liquids"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that liquids on the meat passed the impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If liquids were essential, the משנה would have mentioned them. It mentions only meat.

steps.title: Food makes food impure by rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. By Torah law food does not make food impure, but by rabbinic law it does. The משנה follows the rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, granted that food does not make food impure by Torah law. By rabbinic law, though, it does make it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the liquids answer and gives a different one. The משנה is speaking about a rabbinic level of impurity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only teaches that food does not pass impurity to food on a Torah level. The חכמים added a decree that food does pass impurity to food. So רבי חנינא's case of adding impurity to meat works on a rabbinic level, and the challenge of רבינא is answered.
steps.whatToRemember: Food does not make food impure מדאורייתא, but it does מדרבנן. That is how the משנה can speak of adding impurity to meat.

phrases.english: Rather:

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דְּאֵין אוֹכֶל מְטַמֵּא אוֹכֶל מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: granted that food does not make food impure by Torah law,
by rabbinic law, however, it does make it impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: נְהִי דְּאֵין אוֹכֶל מְטַמֵּא אוֹכֶל מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 15 with a new answer to the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between Torah law and rabbinic law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק says food does not make food impure, the משנה cannot speak of food adding impurity to food.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק applies only to Torah law. By rabbinic decree food does make food impure, and the משנה follows that.

steps.title: Quoting רבי עקיבא's addition in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה, where רבי עקיבא adds a teaching about lighting impure oil in an impure lamp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא added: In all the days of the כהנים, they did not hold back from lighting, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section. It quotes רבי עקיבא's words from the משנה so it can analyze them next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full case in the משנה is תרומה oil that a טבול יום touched, lit in a lamp that a טמא מת touched. The 'etc.' (כו׳) is a shortcut that points the learner back to the rest of the line in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In all the days of the כהנים
Etc., short for the rest of the quote

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva added:
In all the days of the priests
they did not refrain from lighting, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים and opens the discussion of רבי עקיבא's addition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים would light oil that a טבול יום had disqualified in a lamp that a טמא מת had made impure.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא seems to repeat רבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא works out the levels: the oil starts as a שלישי and becomes a שני. That is exactly what רבי חנינא already taught, so what is רבי עקיבא adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now consider: oil that was disqualified by a טבול יום, what level is it? Third. And when he lights it in a lamp made impure by a טמא מת, what level is it? Second. So what is he teaching us? That a third may be made a second? That is the same as that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first counts the levels of impurity in רבי עקיבא's case. Then it uses that count to challenge him: his teaching looks like a repeat of רבי חנינא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום is a שני, so oil he touches becomes a שלישי. A lamp touched by a טמא מת becomes a ראשון, so oil inside it becomes a שני. רבי חנינא already taught that it is allowed to raise something from שלישי to שני, so רבי עקיבא's 'addition' seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who went to the מקוה today but waits for nightfall to be fully pure
A person made impure by a dead body
That is the same as that

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the people with the objects. The טבול יום is a שני and the טמא מת is an אב הטומאה. The oil and the lamp each come out one level lower than whatever touched them.

phrases.english: Now consider:
oil that was disqualified by one who immersed that day,
what is it? Third-degree.
phrases.notes: A טבול יום is a שני, so what he touches is a שלישי.

phrases.english: And when he lights it
in a lamp made impure by one impure from a corpse,
what is it? Second-degree.
phrases.notes: The lamp is a ראשון, so the oil inside it becomes a שני.

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
That a third-degree item may be made second-degree?
That is the same as that!
phrases.notes: Refers to רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים's teaching earlier in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן — שְׁלִישִׁי מוּתָּר לַעֲשׂוֹתוֹ שֵׁנִי, הַיְינוּ הָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the quote from step 18 and challenges whether it teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the levels are counted, רבי עקיבא's case raises a שלישי to a שני. רבי חנינא already taught that, so the 'addition' looks redundant.

steps.title: The case is about a metal lamp
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that רבי עקיבא is speaking about a metal lamp, which has a special status from a פסוק. This passage ends as he starts to quote the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Here we are dealing with a metal lamp, as the Merciful One says:
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה begins to answer the challenge by saying the lamp is made of metal. He is about to bring a פסוק, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A metal object that touches a טמא מת does not drop just one level. The פסוק gives it a much stronger impurity. This makes the lamp more severely impure, so the oil jumps further than from שלישי to שני, and רבי עקיבא's case is a real addition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the special rule for metal objects that touch the dead. That rule explains why רבי עקיבא's teaching is new.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Here we are dealing with a metal lamp,
as the Merciful One states:
phrases.notes: The פסוק is quoted on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19 by identifying the lamp as metal.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a metal lamp
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's case is just a שלישי becoming a שני, the same as רבי חנינא's case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lamp is metal and has a stronger impurity from a פסוק, so רבי עקיבא's case is different and new. The explanation continues on the next amud.
